correctness.rationale: The flag-rank weight is sum of ranks of north-east crossing submatrices of an upper-triangular n-by-n matrix. At total four, a rank-two cut must have adjacent rank-one cuts, and all others zero, forcing a three-index local block with central 2x2 invertible submatrix: (n-2)q^2|GL(2,q)|. Otherwise exactly four rank-one cuts: maximal nonzero superdiagonal 0,1 (single or two disjoint adjacent edges),2,3 yields five disjoint classes, respectively C(n,4)(q-1)^4; (n-1)C(n-2,2)q^2(q-1)^3; C(n-2,2)q^4(q-1)^2; (n-2)(n-3)q^4(q-1)^2; (n-3)q^6(q-1). Direct rank-elimination and complete enumeration over q=2 for n=3,4,5, and q=3 for n=3,4, reproduced each six-class count (including s_2(4,4)=173 and s_3(4,4)=3526). The six-class structural proof is uniform over prime-power q and n>=3. The radius <=4 ball congruence is sum of diagonal-only binomial terms modulo q, yielding C(n-1,4), a NECESSARY condition for nontrivial linear perfect distance-nine codes, not existence.
residual_risks: The exhaustive check did not independently rerun GF(4) tests; proof uses field-independent rank facts and polynomial GL(2,q).
